Riot unveils New Dawn, a major overhaul for League of Legends
At the League of Legends 2026 championship, Riot revealed a new era for League of Legends with a cinematic that's a bit brief on details.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 16, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
Image via Riot Games
The online MOBA League of Legends has been going strong since 2009 and it looks like Riot Games is ready to publicly move the game forward into its next era.
In a video shown during the 2026 League of Legends championship
, head of League Studio Andrei van Roon and executive producer Paul Belleza explain that it's time to move the game to its next evolution, punctuated by a cinematic showing multiple well-known League designs posing over a horizon and finishing with a logo for League of Legends: New Dawn and a January 2027 reveal date.
It's not entirely clear what this "new dawn" entails, but this follows
a 2025 report from Bloomberg News
indicating Riot plans to overhaul
League
to reinvigorate its flagship game. Belleza and van Roon say that a new client is coming alongside it for the first time in ten years, indicating that many of the changes will involve under-the-hood reworkings, but much of the rest is left to supposition and speculation. Riot's own description promises "evolved gameplay," but it's unknown if that is a major overhaul or some gardening around the periphery.

In recent years, Riot has attempted to
expand the property to a broader audience
through initiatives like making a fighting game with the characters in
2XKO
, though that
did not work out as intended
. The company has also toyed with the idea of
making premium titles
, but it is highly unlikely League of Legends would undergo any such dramatic change.
For now, developers will have to wait until January to find out what the "new dawn" of League of Legends looks like in practice.
